facts.text: NESEnv is a Gymnasium environment (class NESEnv(gym.Env))
The action space is Discrete(256), a bitmap of button press values for the 8 NES buttons
The observation space is Box(low=0, high=255, shape=SCREEN_SHAPE_24_BIT, dtype=uint8)
The default observation and the rgb_array render are the zero-copy (240, 256, 3) uint8 RGB screen view
The metadata declares the render modes rgb_array and human and render_fps 60
reset accepts an optional seed and options, calls super().reset(seed=seed) and the native reset, and returns the screen and info
step refuses to run in a done environment, advances the emulator by one frame, and returns the screen, reward, terminated, truncated and info
The base hooks return reward 0, no termination and no truncation unless a subclass overrides them
The reward range is unbounded from -inf to inf
seed() is deprecated in favour of reset(seed=...)
close closes the native emulator and any viewer
render returns the screen in rgb_array mode
dump_state and load_state carry an opaque native snapshot and restore it
get_action_meanings returns ['NOOP'] for the base class

determinism.notes: reset(seed=...) seeds the Gymnasium random generator (nes_env.py:278); the base NESEnv does not use that seed to reset the native emulator (nes_env.py:285), so every reset of the base class starts from the same reset frame and a seed repeats a trajectory. The fake backend also resets to the same start frame.

gaps: the fake is a pure Python stand-in for the native C++ emulator core: it does not emulate the CPU, PPU, mappers, RAM, controllers or audio, and it returns reward 0 with terminated and truncated false like the base NESEnv hooks; it was not compared with the upstream environment
the fake returns a 24 x 32 x 3 uint8 stand-in for the real 240 x 256 x 3 NES frame (docs/ml-observation-fast-paths.md:5-6); the resolution is scaled down to keep receipts small
one tick advances one emulator frame; the declared render_fps is 60 (nes_env.py:54), so timestep_ms is 1000/60; no wall-clock pacing is applied (realtime_factor 0)
snapshot and restore are not offered: NESEnv has dump_state/load_state (nes_env.py:214-225), but the gymnasium bridge publishes a snapshot only for get_state/set_state, which NESEnv does not have
a .nes ROM is required by the upstream constructor and is not supplied; the fake accepts an optional ROM path and does not read it
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the frame state is kept and stays readable
